topic: Visualizing Complex Roots: From Equations to Domain Coloring

sections.title: The Challenge of 2D Equations
lecture_lines: Standard graphs fail for complex functions.
We need four dimensions for mapping inputs.
Visualizing complex roots requires new methods.
animations: #E0E0E0: Draw a standard Cartesian coordinate system.
#FFFF00: Represent 4D mapping using a color-mapped complex surface.
#FF6666: Animate complex roots as specific intersections on the surface.

sections.title: Numerical Root-Finding (Newton's Method)
lecture_lines: It settles precisely into the root.
animations: #E0E0E0: Write the equation z_n+1 = z_n - f(z_n)/f'(z_n).
#FF6666: Create a marble animation rolling on a potential surface.
#FFFF00: Show a trace line converging into the root point.

sections.title: Topological Intuition: The Winding Number
lecture_lines: A loop wraps around the origin.
The winding number detects trapped roots.
No slip, then a root exists.
animations: #FF6666: Animate a closed loop enclosing the origin.
#FFFF00: Illustrate a counter being incremented for each rotation.
#E0E0E0: Visualize a vector pointing from origin to curve.
#77FF77: Display a root appearing inside the loop.
#FF6666: Highlight the total winding count changing to 1.

sections.title: Domain Coloring: Painting the Complex Plane
lecture_lines: Map phase to hue, magnitude to light.
Colors expose roots as bright centers.
animations: #FFFF00: Create a color wheel mapping phase to 0-360 degrees.
#FF6666: Map magnitude to grayscale intensity across the plane.
#77FF77: Render a complex function field using these color rules.
#FF6666: Highlight zero-color singular point at the origin.
#E0E0E0: Pulse the color intensity to emphasize the root center.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
lecture_lines: We synthesize topology and numerical methods.
Visualize using color, pin with Newton.
animations: #E0E0E0: Show summary table comparing numerical and topological methods.
#FFFF00: Animate a winding count indicator next to a colored root.
#77FF77: Final zoom-in on the converged Newton iteration point.
